data.title: IDBI Bank Q2 results: Net profit falls 39% to Rs 2,206 crore, NII jumps 29%; asset quality improves
data.description:
IDBI Bank on Saturday reported a 39.2 percent year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 2,206 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 3,627 crore in the corresponding period last year. However, the lender's net interest income (NII) rose sharply, while gross asset quality improved sequentially.

Net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 28.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 4,227 crore from Rs 3,285 crore in the year-ago quarter.

On the asset quality front, the bank's gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declined by 18 basis points to 2.12 percent at the end of September, compared with 2.30 percent in the preceding quarter.

However, the net NPA ratio edged up by one basis point to 0.17 percent from 0.16 percent in the June quarter.

The latest earnings come just days after the Union Cabinet approved the strategic sale of a 60.72 percent stake in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore, at an acquisition price of Rs 81 per share.

The transaction involves the sale of a 30.48 percent stake held by the central government and a 30.24 percent holding of Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). Following the transaction, the government and LIC will retain a combined 34 percent stake in the lender.

IDBI Bank shares closed at Rs 84.12 on Friday, gaining 0.8 percent for the session. The stock had plunged 7.7 percent on Thursday following the Cabinet's announcement, reversing much of Wednesday's 9 percent rally ahead of the decision.

The stock has declined 19 percent so far in 2026, compared with an 11.5 percent fall in the Nifty 50. IDBI Bank's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 90,449 crore at Friday's close.

data.title: Best of the Week: Jio's big bet beyond telecom
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Jio Platforms Ltd filed its red herring prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) earlier this week, paving the way for what could become India's largest IPO by rupee value. The digital arm of Reliance Industries Ltd is offering 270 million fresh shares at a price band of Rs.1,069-1,119 apiece. At the upper end, the issue is valued at Rs.30,200 crore, or $3.2 billion.

The proposed offering is smaller than the roughly Rs.35,000 crore outlined in its draft papers, reflecting subdued investor appetite amid a prolonged market downturn. At the upper end of the price band, Jio Platforms would command an equity valuation of just over Rs.10 trillion, or about $107 billion, below the $133 billion valuation analysts estimated in January.

The IPO opens for subscription on 21 October and closes on 23 October, with listing scheduled for 28 October. It would surpass Hyundai Motor India's Rs.27,870 crore offering in rupee terms, although Hyundai remains ahead in dollar terms. Jio plans to use part of the proceeds to prepay borrowings at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.

The company reported a revenue of about Rs.1.47 trillion and net profit of Rs.30,053 crore in fiscal year 2026 (FY26), up 14.5% and 15%, respectively. It has more than 524 million active subscribers and counts Meta, Google and several global private equity firms among its investors.

Beyond the SIM card

Jio's IPO will test more than investor appetite for a large telecom business. It will also show whether the market is willing to pay a premium for the wider digital ecosystem that Mukesh Ambani has spent a decade building.

Since its launch in 2016, when free voice calls and cheap data disrupted India's telecom market, Jio has expanded internet access and become the country's largest operator. Its subscriber base exceeds Bharti Airtel's, but Airtel earns more per user, highlighting Jio's challenge: turning scale into stronger earnings.

The next phase of growth rests on artificial intelligence (AI), enterprise services and digital applications. Reliance is building AI capabilities through Reliance Intelligence, a joint venture with Meta, while Jio is developing enterprise tools and partnerships to deepen customer engagement and find new sources of revenue.

The listing will also give investors a clearer way to value Jio's telecom and digital businesses separately from RIL's oil, retail and other operations. However, RIL shareholders will receive neither cash nor direct Jio shares from the fresh issue. Any benefit to the parent company will depend on whether the listing unlocks value in its retained 66.43% stake.

For new investors, the central question is whether Jio can monetise its enormous subscriber base through AI and digital services, rather than relying primarily on telecom growth.

India's bullet train takes shape

India's first bullet train corridor is entering its final construction phase, with services expected to begin in stages from 2027. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad project combines Japanese Shinkansen technology, European signalling and indigenous BEML trainsets. But costs have nearly doubled to Rs.1.98 trillion, while delays and questions over affordability persist. Its biggest test is whether the technology and expertise gained can make future high-speed rail projects faster and cheaper.

Nifty profits set for a 23% jump

Nifty 50 companies are expected to post 23% year-on-year profit growth in Q2FY27, their strongest in four quarters, as metals, banks and auto exporters lead gains. Lower crude prices helped in July and August, but September's surge to $109 a barrel could raise costs in coming quarters. Rising input prices threaten margins across consumer goods, vehicles and cement. While resilient urban demand may support festive sales, rural consumption remains uncertain.

Most brokerages expect FY27 profit growth of 14-15%, though Elara Securities has cut its forecast to 11%, citing a tougher second half.

TVS siblings' inheritance feud

The TVS family dispute centres on whether a restructuring left siblings Lakshmi and Sudarshan Venu with unequal business inheritances. Lakshmi now heads the smaller auto-parts business, while Sudarshan controls TVS Motor and the group's lending arms. Since the 2022-23 changes, TVS Motor's revenue has surged 76%, while Sundaram-Clayton's revenue has stagnated, intensifying questions over the fairness of the split.

Hyundai and TVS eye Tata's Ace with an electric mini truck

Hyundai and TVS are about to take their partnership from three wheels to four. After formalizing their electric three-wheeler tie-up in April, the two companies are reportedly preparing an electric mini truck to take on Tata Motors' Ace, with a 2027 rollout in sight. Their three-wheeler is already being tested on the streets of Gurugram.

The timing makes sense. Electric truck and light commercial vehicle registrations hit 16,995 in the first half of this fiscal, already beating all of last year's. Tata Motors and Euler lead the pack. Hyundai and TVS would be entering a crowded lane.

The green card freeze on Indian IT

Washington says Indian IT firms have misused the green card route. But the numbers tell a different story. The US has frozen PERM labour certificates for eight firms, including TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Cognizant, citing roughly 100,000 certifications as proof of lost American jobs. But Mint's analysis of 17 years of data shows India's Big Five got under 58,000 of 1.45 million certifications, about 4% of the total. Their share has slid from around 10% to below 1%.

Meanwhile, Amazon, Microsoft and Google each collected tens of thousands. TCS and Infosys say they expect little impact, having already moved away from this route.

How India's IT majors fared in Q2

The IT earnings season has opened, and the scorecards could hardly look more different. TCS grew just 0.2% to $7.64 billion, its slowest second quarter in three years, with margins stuck at 24%. Wipro slipped 0.1% to $2.61 billion, its second straight quarterly decline. Yet HCLTech grew 2% to $3.72 billion, helped by AI revenue that jumped 28% sequentially, while Tech Mahindra, riding a big telecom deal, posted its fastest September-quarter growth in three years.

Same cautious demand backdrop, very different results. What set the winners apart? And is TCS's growth-over-margin trade-off a smart bet or a worrying sign?

Why IDBI Bank shares love Wednesdays

IDBI Bank's shares seem to have a favourite day of the week, and a day they dread. Over the past year, Wednesday has delivered the stock's best average return, 1.08%, while Thursday has pulled it back by 0.8%. Five of its ten biggest single-day jumps, including a 17% surge in June, also came on a Wednesday. Investors appear to be betting on privatization news from Union cabinet meetings, which are usually held midweek.

This week, the pattern played out almost perfectly. The stock rose nearly 9% on Wednesday, then fell 8.1% on Thursday, wiping out almost all of those gains. Is it coincidence or clockwork?

The IMF's good news for India comes with a catch

India got a growth upgrade from the International Monetary Fund, and the headline looks great. The fine print is where it gets interesting. The fund now sees the economy growing 7% this fiscal year, up from 6.5%. Yet India was not the only country to get a boost, and a weaker rupee is taking a bite out of the bigger picture.

Measured in dollars, growth looks closer to 4%, and India has slipped to sixth place in the global GDP ranking, behind the UK. That puts the long-promised $5 trillion milestone under strain. The latest projections suggest India could narrowly miss it.

data.title: Anirudh Ravichander-Kavya Maran wedding: Greece nuptials, Chennai reception - What we know so far
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- It's official! Music composer Anirudh Ravichander and Sunrisers Hyderabad CEO Kavya Maran are getting married this November.

While the couple themselves have remained tight-lipped about the wedding, a formal invitation extended by the Maran family to Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has confirmed a grand Chennai reception.

According to entertainment portal Valai Pechu, Anirudh and Kavya are expected to tie the knot in a picturesque destination wedding in Greece on November 11.

While preparations are reportedly in full swing, neither the music composer nor Kavya Maran has officially issued a public statement confirming the nuptials.

Following the ceremony in Greece, the couple will host a grand reception at a five-star hotel in Chennai. While initial reports indicated the event was scheduled for November 14, an update from the Telangana CMO confirmed it has been moved to November 21.

The exact reason for the rescheduling remains undisclosed.

Telangana CMO said on X: "Sun Group Chairman Kalanithi Maran and his wife, Kavery Maran, met Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy at his residence in Jubilee Hills and invited him to the wedding reception of their daughter, Kavya Maran."

"The wedding reception of Kavya Maran and Anirudh Ravichander is scheduled to be held in Chennai on November 21. #KalanithiMaran #KavyaMaran," it added.

According to a Times of India report, the guest list is expected to be studded with VIPs, considering the Maran family's deep ties to both business and politics, and Anirudh's massive footprint in the film industry.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister 'Thalapathy' Vijay is reportedly among the prominent dignitaries invited to the celebrations. TOI report indicated that the formal wedding invitations have already been dispatched.

Kavya Maran is the daughter of Kalanithi Maran and serves as the co-owner and head of Sunrisers Hyderabad. She also oversees Sunrisers Eastern Cape in the SA20 League and Sunrisers Leeds in The Hundred, besides being the Executive Director of Sun TV Network Limited.

Anirudh Ravichander rose to fame with his debut song "Why This Kolaveri Di" featuring Dhanush in 2012. The song became a national obsession overnight, with over 450 million views on YouTube.

He composed his first film album at the age of 15, making him the youngest music director in India. By 18, he was already composing music for Tamil superstars, including Rajinikanth, Vijay, and Sivakarthikeyan.

In 2022, Anirudh made his full-fledged debut in Hindi cinema with Shah Rukh Khan and Atlee's Jawan. He previously composed singles for Bollywood movies David and Jersey.

Anirudh has already won 2 Filmfare Awards South, 10 SIIMA Awards, 6 Edison Awards and 5 Vijay Awards.

data.title: Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact Review: Is this air purifier perfect for bedrooms and studies?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- No longer a seasonal inconvenience, air pollution is part of everyday life thanks to year-round construction dust and traffic fumes. The Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact ( Rs.7,999) from Xiaomi's Mijia sub-brand arrives in time to make cleaner indoor air accessible without commandeering your living room. it's small, relatively affordable and packs some smarts, but can it punch above its weight to get the job done?

At 35.5cm tall and 22cm wide, the Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact is rather easy to accommodate, and its compact dimensions allows it to fit just about anywhere, from a bedside table to a small patch of floor space. It's lightweight at 2.2kg, and can be moved between rooms easily, although for something this portable, the absence of a carry handle is a minor niggle.

Placed on the floor, the white cylindrical design is understated and functional, with a perforated lower section that draws in air and a circular grille on top that sends purified air back into the room. A touch-sensitive panel with controls for power, operating modes and display brightness, and a colour-coded air-quality indicator, round off the minimalist design. Just remember not to tuck it away behind furniture or in a tight corner; the purifier needs the air inlets and outlet unobstructed to draw air in and circulate the cleaned air out.

Having lived with Mijia products for years, I knew what to expect: a product that gets the basics right, with plenty of thoughtful little touches and smart flourishes thrown in for good measure. The Purifier 4 Compact doesn't disappoint on that front, and its smart features feel genuinely useful rather than like a checklist of things a connected appliance is expected to offer.

Through the Xiaomi Home app, you can control the purifier remotely, switch modes, set schedules and timers, and create automations. There's support for Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant for voice control, and a child lock prevents accidental changes to the settings. The app also lets users know when the filter needs replacing, taking some of the guesswork out of maintenance. And of course, while it can be operated using its onboard controls, the app is handy for finer control over fan speed. One drawback is that while air quality can be discerned via the green, yellow, orange and red colour-coded indicators, the lack of detailed numerical readings and historical trends is a missed opportunity.

The Purifier 4 Compact uses a three-stage filtration system-a pre-filter for larger particles such as dust and hair, a HEPA filter for finer airborne particles, and an activated carbon layer for odours-claiming to remove up to 99.97% of particles as small as 0.3 microns, including dust, smoke, pet dander and pollen. With a respectable-for-its-size particle Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR), rated at 230 cubic metres per hour, the air purifier is most effective in smaller spaces such as bedrooms and study rooms, although Xiaomi says it can be used in rooms over 400 square feet as well. Larger rooms may benefit from a more powerful unit, while a smaller unit like this one will take longer to clean the air.

In practice, the purifier's biggest strength is its ability to work away in the background, and the 27W power rating makes it practical for extended use without resulting in a large electricity bill. Just leave it in Auto mode and its sensor adjusts the fan speed according to the detected air quality, spinning up when pollution levels rise and settling down once things improve.

One can hear it working harder when the air needs attention, but it's generally unobtrusive, particularly in a bedroom or home office. Sleep mode is even quieter, with a claimed noise level of just 20dB and the option to switch off the display. One caveat: the activated carbon filter takes a while to deal with strong cooking odours or incense.

At Rs.7,999, the Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact is an appealing entry point into air purification, or if you're looking for a second (or third) air purifier beyond the one in the living room. It's quiet, compact, easy to operate and sensibly equipped with smart controls. Its cleaning capacity is modest, the air-quality reporting basic and the odour removal nothing to write home about, but at this price, these feel more like reasonable compromises than dealbreakers.

Tushar Kanwar is a tech columnist and commentator, and tweets @2shar.

New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently hiked its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on 7 October 2026. This announcement was made at the culmination of the three-day Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting.

Subsequently, several banks have also increased their repo-linked lending rates, thus making loans linked to these benchmarks potentially more expensive. Prominent lending institutions such as State Bank of India (SBI), Punjab National Bank (PNB), Bank of India, Indian Bank, Bank of Baroda and Canara Bank have revised their respective lending benchmarks in October 2026.

Due to these developments, existing borrowers and those planning to take fresh home loans should diligently check the latest rates, as changes in lending benchmarks can impact borrowing costs and monthly instalments. New borrowers and fresh loan applicants may also face higher borrowing costs due to these changes.

Still, do keep in mind that the revised benchmark is not necessarily the final interest rate the borrower pays. data.title: Swiggy share price: Down 50% in 1 year; can food delivery stock recover? Should you buy the dip? Check target, stop-loss
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Swiggy shares have come under significant pressure over the past year, raising questions about whether the food delivery and quick-commerce company can stage a sustained recovery.

While improving profitability in its core food delivery business and efforts to reduce quick-commerce losses have strengthened the fundamental investment case, the stock's technical structure remains weak.

In the previous session, the stock ended 2% higher at Rs.234.05. It is now 49% away from its 52-week high of Rs.460, hit in October 2025 and its 52-week low of Rs.228.50, hit in in the previous session, October 16, 2026.

It has been under pressure recently, down 13% in 1 month, 14% in 3 months, 16% in 6 months and around 50% in the last 1 year.

Recently, domestic brokerage house Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers upgraded Swiggy to Buy, retaining its target price of Rs.310, implying a potential upside of over 32%. However, technical analyst Jigar S Patel has advised caution, identifying key support and breakout levels that could determine the stock's next move.

Anand Rathi said Swiggy was moving from a phase in which growth came at the expense of profitability towards one in which growth could increasingly support earnings. The brokerage highlighted the recovery in contribution margin, which improved from a loss of around 5.6% in Q4FY25 to contribution break-even in Q1FY27.

"The core Food Delivery segment continued to serve as primary profit generator. The segment recorded steady EBITDA margin of ~3.1% on a strong ~17.4% YoY expansion in GOV in Q1FY27," Anand Rathi said in its October 16 research report.

Anand Rathi expects food delivery to record annual GOV growth of 18-20% over FY26-FY28, alongside further margin expansion.

The brokerage also expects cash flows from food delivery, together with treasury income, to cover operational losses from quick commerce by FY28 or the first half of FY29. Swiggy had a cash balance of approximately Rs.140 billion in Q1FY27, according to the report.

Instamart's planned shift towards a direct inventory-led model is another potential profitability driver. Anand Rathi estimates that this transition could add Rs.4-5 per order to contribution margin, equivalent to an improvement of around 80-100 basis points. Instamart is also focusing on improving asset efficiency and expanding higher-margin non-grocery categories, which accounted for approximately 30% of its business, the brokerage said.

Anand Rathi retained its Rs.310 target price, valuing the food delivery business at 30 times estimated FY28 adjusted EBITDA, at an approximately 15% discount to Zomato. The brokerage said Swiggy's current valuation was attractive because investors were effectively getting exposure to quick commerce and dining-out without paying a significant additional premium.

"Considering attractive valuation at the CMP, we upgrade our rating on Swiggy to BUY with an unrevised TP of Rs310, assuming 30x FY28e adj. EBITDA to FD (~15% discount to Zomato)," Anand Rathi said.

However, the brokerage flagged intense competition and slower food delivery growth amid a consumption slowdown as key risks.

Meanwhile, on the technical front, Jigar S Patel said Swiggy's daily chart showed a weak technical structure, with the stock trading below all its key moving averages. This indicated that the prevailing trend remained under pressure and that the recovery lacked sufficient confirmation. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) had entered oversold territory, pointing to intensified selling pressure, although Patel cautioned that an oversold reading did not guarantee an immediate reversal.

"The stock may attempt to establish a base in the Rs.225-240 zone, which will be crucial to watch for signs of stabilisation," Patel said, highlighting the range as an important area for investors to monitor.

According to Patel, a sustained breakout above Rs.255 would be needed to signal a meaningful improvement in momentum and strengthen the possibility of a recovery. Until the stock forms a stable base and crosses this level, he recommended a wait-and-watch approach rather than aggressive fresh buying.

For traders, the Rs.225-240 zone is the key support area identified by Patel, while Rs.255 is the technical breakout threshold. A confirmed stop-loss level was not specified in his commentary, so investors should avoid treating either the support zone or the breakout level as a formal stop-loss recommendation.

Swiggy's outlook therefore presents two contrasting signals: Anand Rathi's positive fundamental view and Patel's caution on the charts. Investors should consider their time horizon and risk tolerance, monitor whether the stock stabilises around support, and look for a sustained move above Rs.255 before interpreting the price action as a confirmed recovery.

data.title: ISL 2026-27: Can the new club-led model for Indian football succeed?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- It was a good day for a new beginning. The late afternoon sun shone brightly as Bengaluru FC took on SC Delhi in the season-opener of the Indian Super League 2026-27 at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium on 10 October. Over 10,000 fans were in attendance at the stadium and over 7 million watched it on YouTube as the hosts rallied from 1-2 down, scoring in the 89th minute to edge to a 3-2 win.

Echoing the theme in the promos that went with #WeAreOpen, the ISL was well and truly open for business.

"It's a fresh start," says Mandar Tamhane, the CEO of NorthEast United FC and a former manager of the Indian men's national team. With the ISL undergoing major structural changes, there is optimism. "We now have a club-led model in place, which is a first ever in Indian football. The consortium of 13 clubs (participating in ISL 2026-27) controls the league's commercial interests," he adds. The AIFF is involved in governance and entitled to 10% of the net profit.

"It means whether it's the broadcaster or sponsors, all these things will now be in the hands of the clubs to decide the way forward and how to structure it. Collectively, the 13 owners of ISL are the single largest investors annually in Indian football, so their interests have to be protected. If their fate is now in their own hands by virtue of the club-led model, they can structure the league to maximise the commercial side of the sport."

India's top division football league has rarely been built on a commercially sound and sustainable business plan. The first national league came into being in 1996, when the All India Football Federation (AIFF) launched the National Football League (NFL). In 2007, it was rebranded as the I-League, which struggled to survive in an increasingly market-driven world.

The ISL pulled Indian football out of the trenches and launched it into orbit in 2014. Marquee signings, prime-time games and celebrity sightings added glamour to India's top-tier competition. For 12 years, AIFF's commercial partners, Reliance-IMG's Football Sports Development Ltd (FSDL), pumped money into the league, paying AIFF fees of Rs.50 crore per year.

As their contract with AIFF ended in December 2025, the league battled for survival. A truncated 2025-26 season took place from February to May this year, with only a single round-robin format, mainly to keep up the continuity. After that began the rebuild. Over discussions with AIFF, a club-led model for ISL was accepted, giving the owners agency over the product.

"When the commercial partner decided not to continue, it was a Herculean task to figure out what's next," Tamhane says. "It was an eye-opener and led to the collective decision not to seek another partner, but rather take control of the commercial entity ourselves with AIFF support."

Even after that, Indian football took a few hits. Tata Steel-backed Jamshedpur FC bowed out from ISL and sold their licence for a token fee of Rs.100 to Churchill Brothers, and Diamond Harbour, which was promoted to the top division, failed to pay their participation fee of Rs.1.1 crore. Since they are unable to compete, Diamond Harbour will drop down at the end of the season, shielding the other clubs from relegation.

On a more positive note, ISL roped in a title sponsor and combined a traditional broadcast deal with free streaming of all games on YouTube.

After all the machinations in the boardroom, what we now have is a full-league season, complete with its home-and-away round-robin format followed by the six-team playoffs. While the team topping the table after the round-robin stage will win the Shield, the cup will be awarded to the last club standing after the playoffs.

"In the beginning of the season, everyone is excited and hopeful, though there are still big differences (this time)," Manolo Marquez, former India coach and current Mumbai City FC coach, said at the pre-tournament press conference.

"Home-and-away competition over a long tournament is the most fair format. It's a pity Diamond Harbour couldn't play and that it's 13 teams instead of 14, but playing 24 games will be a good opportunity. It will be a good fight among many teams fighting to enter the top six."

On 10 October, Bengaluru and Delhi set the ball rolling with an entertaining contest that offered end-to-end action, comeback drama and redemption. Dutch defender Menno Koch's first dent on ISL was an own goal in the 32nd minute that helped the visitors to a 2-1 lead, but it was Koch who scored Bengaluru's late winner.

While all the goals were netted by foreigners in the match, two Indian players made the headlines. Diamond Singh became the league's youngest debutant, at 16 years and 119 days, when he came on as a substitute. For Bengaluru, Soham Varshneya, 22, proved to be the game changer. Brought on in the 73rd minute, Varshneya's fresh legs and fresh ideas tipped the match in Bengaluru's favour.

In Guwahati, NorthEast United edged past recently crowned IFA Shield champions Mohun Bagan 1-0 with an added time (90+2) winner from Jithin MS.

Even though the league continues to depend on foreigners, especially in forward positions, young Indian talent has started making some headway. Inter Kashi has taken that idea, opting to go in with an all-Indian 22-member squad at the start of the season. Though their decision was mainly influenced by the Fifa transfer-registration ban, it is a bold move for the club trying to carve an identity.

"Since there is no relegation, why should we not, for the love of our country, play Indian strikers and see if they can perform?" club CEO Prithijit Das said after their opening match on 11 October.

"I don't remember the last time, apart from (Sunil) Chhetri, that Indian strikers played back-to-back matches for 90 minutes. Ayush Chikara was a great prospect. Manvir Singh was a great prospect, but they could not get the time. Maybe with Inter Kashi, they get the time, maybe things can change."

There were no instant rewards for the radical approach, as Kerala Blasters handed them a 2-0 defeat.

Match week 1 already delivered some interesting battles and sprung a few surprises. FC Goa's growing rivalry with Chennaiyin FC ended in a hard-fought 1-1 draw, while Churchill Brothers announced their ISL arrival with a 2-1 win over former champions Mumbai City FC.

Indian football had tried bigger and better and come unstuck. ISL 2.0 is a more realistic, restrained version of the sports league, not dictating, but discovering its place in the sun.

Deepti Patwardhan is a sportswriter based in Mumbai.

data.title: Finance Ministry says Centre allowed to sell stake in IDBI Bank, refers Delhi HC's 2018 judgement to defend dilution
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The Finance Ministry in an official statement today, 17 October, clarified legislative developments concerning the Centre's shareholding in IDBI Bank and defended its dilution plan for the lender.

The PIB release reiterated that during the discussions of Union Budget, 2003 and the parliamentary debate on the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, an amendment seeking to restrict the dilution of the government's stake was moved but was ultimately rejected and did not form part of the enacted legislation.

It added that the matter was subsequently examined by the Delhi High Court in All India IDBI Officers' Association v. Union of India & Others decided on 17 December 2018. It said the judgement did not preclude the Centre from diluting its stake and statements made before the House cannot override a statue enacted by the Parliament.

According to the release, the High Court, while dismissing the writ petition, adjudicated in paragraphs 41 and 42 as follows:

"This Court is of the view that the statements made before the House almost 15 years earlier, in a debate relating to a legislative activity, would not preclude the Central Government from diluting its stake in IDBI Ltd."

"Indisputably, the legislation enacted by the Parliament after the debate did not contain the amendment that was sought to be introduced. The statements made before the House cannot substitute or override the statue so enacted by the Parliament. Surely, the Parliament was conscious of the import of not including the proviso as proposed."

"The principles of promissory estoppel are wholly inapplicable in the aforesaid context. It is not possible to accept that the statements made in Parliament amounted to a representation made to the employees and they had acted to their prejudice based on such representation. The statements made before the House were in the context of enacting a legislation (the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003), and the said Act has to be interpreted in conformity with the settled principles of statutory interpretation."

"There is no ambiguity in the language of the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003 and there is no scope to read any provision into the said enactment which proscribes the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd."

As per the ministry, the Delhi HC judgment is significant "as it specifically addresses the doctrine of promissory estoppel, which was relied upon in challenging the Government's decision to dilute its shareholding".

"The doctrine could not be invoked to prevent the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI," it added.

As per the statement, the HC judgment dated 17 December 2018, "clarifies beyond doubt that the doctrine of promissory estoppel cannot be invoked on the basis of statements made during parliamentary debates to restrict the Government's power to dilute its shareholding in the IDBI Bank Ltd."

The Court further held that the enacted legislation contained no prohibition against reducing the Government's stake in the IDBI Bank, it added.

It added that the Centre's policy to transformation and strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank was reiterated in successive Union Budget Speeches in the Parliament as follows:

As per the ministry, the legislative history of the IDBI Act, Delhi HC's judicial pronouncement and successive Budget speeches collectively demonstrate the evolution of the Centre's policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank.

Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings will acquire a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank for about Rs.53,000 crore ($5.5 billion), in what would be the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank, PTI reported on 14 October.

The deal was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), which approved Fairfax as strategic buyer for the government's 30.48% stake (for about Rs.26,620 crore) and state-run Life Insurance Corporation of India's (LIC) 30.24% (for about Rs.26,440 crore).

The sale process began in 2022 and faced a setback earlier this year when initial bids fell below the government's reserve price. Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa-led Fairfax will pay Rs.81/share, higher than the benchmark fair value of Rs.75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies, an official statement said.

The transaction still needs approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which will conduct a "fit and proper" assessment, as well as the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and other statutory authorities.

data.title: Dividend alert: IRFC, Tech Mahindra, ICICI Prudential AMC, among 11 stocks to watch next week: Check record date, payout
data.description:
Dividend Stocks, Oct. 17 -- Investors tracking dividend income have several stocks to watch next week, with 11 companies scheduled to have record dates between October 21 and October 23, 2026. The list includes Tech Mahindra, LTM, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, MRPL, Angel One, Tips Music, IRFC and ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company, among others.

The announced dividend amounts range from Rs.0.50 per share for Elecon Engineering Company to Rs.30 per share for ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company. However, investors should pay attention to the record dates and eligibility requirements before making investment decisions.

A dividend is a portion of a company's profits or distributable reserves paid to shareholders. Companies may distribute dividends as a way to share earnings with investors, with the amount generally declared on a per-share basis.

The record date is the date on which a company checks its shareholder records to determine who is eligible to receive the dividend. Investors need to account for the applicable settlement cycle and ex-dividend date when buying shares. Simply purchasing a stock on its record date does not necessarily make an investor eligible for the payout.

Investors should therefore check the relevant stock exchange announcements and ensure that their purchases meet the eligibility requirements. A dividend announcement also does not guarantee that a stock's market price will remain unchanged, as share prices can move in response to market conditions and dividend-related adjustments.

Here are the 11 companies, their scheduled record dates and the dividend amounts per share, based on the supplied list.

1. ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Ltd

ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company has a record date of October 21, 2026, for a dividend of Rs.30 per share. This is the highest per-share payout among the 11 companies listed.

Earlier in FY27, ICICI Prudential had declared a final dividend of Rs.12.40 per share for FY2026, with an ex-date and record date of June 12, 2026.

LTM has scheduled a dividend of Rs.25 per share, with October 23, 2026, as the record date, and the dividend will be paid within 30 days of declaration. The IT company had also paid a final dividend of Rs.53 per share in May 2026.

This takes its dividend distribution over the trailing 12 months to Rs.75 per share.

Tech Mahindra has announced a dividend of Rs.15 per share, with October 23, 2026, as the record date. The company has also announced a 1:1 bonus issue. The dividend will be paid on or before November 13, 2026.

In its previous major dividend distribution, Tech Mahindra paid a final dividend of Rs.36 per share, with July 3, 2026, as the ex-dividend date.

360 ONE WAM has announced a dividend of Rs.7.50 per share, with October 23, 2026, as the record date. The dividend will be paid or dispatched on or before November 13, subject to applicable taxes.

The wealth management company had previously paid a dividend of Rs.4.50 per share during the May 2026 payout cycle.

ICICI Lombard General Insurance has announced a dividend of Rs.7 per share, with October 23, 2026, as the record date. The interim dividend will be paid on or before Thursday, November 12, 2026.

The insurer's previous final dividend was Rs.6 per share, with June 2026 as the ex-dividend period.

Tips Music has announced a dividend of Rs.6.50 per share, with October 22, 2026, as the record date. The dividend will be paid on or before November 12, 2026.

The company had previously paid a final dividend of Rs.10.50 per share, with June 9, 2026, as the ex-dividend date.

7. Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL)

MRPL has scheduled a dividend of Rs.3 per share, with October 21, 2026, as the record date. The interim dividend will be paid to eligible shareholders on or before November 4, 2026.

Earlier in March 2026, the company declared an interim dividend of Rs.4 per share, which went ex-dividend on March 11.

HDB Financial Services has announced an interim dividend of Rs.2 per share for the financial year 2026-27, with October 23, 2026, as the record date. Dividend payout date is not mentioned in the exchange filing.

It did not pay any dividend in the previous quarter.

Angel One has announced a dividend of Rs.1.40 per share, with October 22, 2026, as the record date. No dividend payout datee was mentioned in the exchange filing.

The brokerage announced the payout as its second interim dividend for the financial year on October 15, 2026. It had previously paid an interim dividend of Rs.1 per share in July 2026 and Rs.1.75 per share in March 2026.

Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) has announced a dividend of Rs.1.15 per share, with October 23, 2026, as the record date. This was also the Navratna PSU's highest-ever dividend declared.

IRFC dividend will be paid to eligible shareholders within 30 days from the date of its declaration to those shareholder.

IRFC had previously paid an interim dividend of Rs.1.05 per share in March 2026, with March 13 as the ex-dividend date. The latest payout is Rs.0.10 per share higher than the previous one.

Elecon Engineering has announced a dividend of Rs.0.50 per share, with October 21, 2026, as the record date. This interim dividend will be paid to all shareholders on or after Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the company said in its exchange filing.

The company had previously declared a final dividend of Rs.1.50 per share, with June 12, 2026, as the ex-dividend date.

data.title: MSCI Tightens Index Rules As Strategy And Other Bitcoin Treasury Firms Face Fresh Scrutiny
data.description:
TL;DR: MSCI has revised its methodology for classifying non-operating companies, putting Bitcoin-heavy treasury businesses under closer index scrutiny. Any possible exclusion of companies such as Strategy must be assessed against the actual screening criteria and protections for existing index constituents.

One of the most important questions facing publicly listed Bitcoin treasury companies may no longer be about Bitcoin’s price. It may be about whether index providers consider them operating businesses at all.

MSCI announced changes to the rules governing eligibility for its Global Investable Market Indexes on October 15. The methodology is intended to distinguish companies conducting substantial operating activities from those functioning primarily as investment vehicles.

Strategy, the Michael Saylor-led business that has raised enormous sums to purchase Bitcoin, is an obvious company for investors to watch. But the new rules do not mean Strategy has already been removed from MSCI indexes.

The Financial Tests That Matter

Under the revised approach, balance-sheet composition is only the beginning. MSCI also examines operating and financial characteristics before determining whether a business falls within the non-operating classification.

That distinction matters because businesses holding digital assets can still have genuine operating activities. A large Bitcoin treasury does not by itself establish an immediate exclusion under the entire methodology.

MSCI has also outlined safeguards for existing constituents. These are intended to reduce abrupt changes when companies move between eligibility classifications.

Why Index Membership Matters

MSCI benchmarks underpin investment decisions at institutions worldwide. When a company leaves a major benchmark, funds tracking it may need to adjust their holdings even if they remain bullish about the business.

For Bitcoin treasury firms, such an adjustment would be separate from developments on the blockchain or movements in their Bitcoin reserves. It would be driven by their treatment within conventional equity indexes.

The November index review should provide clearer answers about the practical consequences. Until then, treating any specific company’s removal as a completed event would go further than MSCI’s announcement supports.

data.title: Apple's iPhone Duo Demand Tracking 'Solidly Out Of The Gate', Says Analyst As AAPL Stock Caps Off Best Week Since September Launch
data.description:
Key points:
  • Evercore cautioned, however, that extended lead times can reflect either strong demand or constrained supply.
  • The firm noted that the new form factor could create tighter supply during the initial launch period.
  • Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster said the latest delivery times are making him more confident in his 20 million-unit iPhone Duo estimate for fiscal 2027.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) is getting an early read on demand for its new iPhone Duo, with initial delivery estimates extending well into January shortly after pre-orders opened.

The early demand signals come as Apple shares capped their strongest week since the iPhone Duo launch, with the stock rising over 2% this week, following a nearly 4% rise during the iPhone launch week in September.

Apple shares ended with a gain of 0.4% in Friday’s regular trade, but edged lower by 0.2% in the afterhours session.

iPhone Duo Delivery Dates Stretch Into January

According to TheFly, Evercore ISI said iPhone Duo delivery dates quickly pushed out to late January, or roughly 100 days, across all regions and configurations it tracks, after pre-orders began Friday.

The firm views the development as positive for Apple, saying demand is tracking “solidly out of the gate.”

Evercore cautioned, however, that extended lead times can reflect either strong demand or constrained supply. The firm noted that the new form factor could create tighter supply during the initial launch period.

Meanwhile, lead times for the iPhone Pro and Pro Max remain “generally stable to shorter” as Apple works through its launch orders, according to Evercore.

The firm maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating and $380 price target on Apple shares.

Gene Munster Sees Early Signal For 20M iPhone Duo Units

Meanwhile, Deepwater Asset Management's Gene Munster said in a series of posts on X that iPhone Duo lead times had stabilized at Jan. 25, 2027 as of 1:30 p.m. ET on Friday.

Munster said he expects some volatility in the delivery estimates over the next several days but remains encouraged by the initial signal.

“Even factoring in supply will be tight with the new form factor, I still believe the early read is positive vs expectations.”

Munster said the latest delivery times are making him more confident in his 20 million-unit iPhone Duo estimate for fiscal 2027, compared with a Street estimate of 10 million units.

At 20 million units, Munster estimates the Duo could account for roughly 8% of Apple's overall iPhone unit sales next year. He also highlighted just how unusual the current lead times are based on his long history tracking Apple's launches.

Munster, however, emphasized the key caveat: Apple’s production capacity remains unknown. He ultimately sees the long lead times as evidence that the new iPhone is off to a fast start, even while acknowledging that supply constraints tied to the new form factor could be contributing to the wait.

“While we don’t know supply which is lower because of new form factor, the long lead times suggest we’re off to a fast start,” Munster concluded.

iPhone 18 Pro Demand Cools, But Pro Max Holds Up

In an update last week, Munster said iPhone 18 Pro lead times have fallen sharply after starting well ahead of the iPhone 17 Pro.

Across eight countries, lead times were initially 15% longer than last year's model, remained 15% higher after one week and then fell to 5% below the year-ago level after two weeks, according to Munster.

“Going into the cycle, I predicted we would see lead times 20% lower than last year given the carrot of the new Duo would pull former Pro buyers up to the Duo,” he said.

Munster noted that the iPhone 18 Pro Max has held up better, with lead times now roughly in line with last year’s model after initially running 18% longer. He called that a “win” for Apple, estimating that as many as 20% of last year’s early Pro Max buyers could be waiting for the Duo.

What Retail Traders Think Of AAPL Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Apple trended in the ‘extremely bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

AAPL stock is up 26% year-to-date and 39% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is up 16% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 18%.

data.title: Grandparents Become Caregivers as Childcare Costs Soar — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Alice Kantor

Rebecca Maier, a 41-year-old healthcare professional in Seattle, faced a child-care crisis when her first child was born in 2020.

Her in-laws relocated to Seattle from Texas to look after her toddler. In exchange, Maier and her husband started giving them a $1,000 monthly stipend.

"A thousand dollars a month is a fraction of what we would pay for full-time infant child-care that runs around $3,200 a month at a Bright Horizons type of center," Maier says.

She isn't alone.

Increasingly, grandparents are asked to step in to look after children. The U.S. Census estimated that 6.1 million children under 18 were living under a grandparent's roof in 2020, up from 5.8 million in 2010.

Some 45 million grandparents contribute an average of over 500 hours of care annually, according to a 2026 survey by AARP. The seniors organization estimated the value of unpaid care at $731 billion, double what it had been in 2006.

Grandparents move across states to be closer to young families. They often stop working or cut back on hobbies.

Some grandparents get paid for their labor. While family dynamics traditionally emphasize unpaid aid, setting up a formal or semiformal financial arrangement can help grandparents feel genuinely valued and establish healthier boundaries between loved ones, experts say.

Madonna Harrington Meyer, a sociology professor at Syracuse University in New York and author of "Grandmothers at Work," says the increased reliance on grandparents for child-care exacts physical, social, emotional and financial tolls.

"Some grandparents are not physically able to provide as much care for grandchildren as parents might wish," she says. "Many grandparents told me they are spending far too much time with parenting hats on, and wish they could put their grandparenting hats on."

The burden can also be financial, with lower-income grandparents forgoing medical or dental care in some cases to pay for grandchildren's needs.

Yet, despite these hindrances, formal financial compensation is rare, she says.

Most grandparents refuse payment to help adult children save money or to avoid turning familial love into an employee-employer dynamic, she says.

Families will instead turn to informal strategies such as giving money to cover rent, car repairs or medical bills.

"Generally pay is under the table, with no Social Security or paid time off, which may not be in the best interest of grandparents," she says.

Natalie Renew, executive director of Philadelphia-based fund-raising group Home Grown, an association focused on improving home-based child-care, says the primary challenge in the U.S. stems from escalating living costs, such as food and gasoline.

About 39 U.S. states now offer some form of public subsidy to support relative caregivers, but those tend to be restricted to full-time carers and specific circumstances, such as children exiting the foster care system.

"Few grandparents can access child care subsidies, and the safety net for food and housing benefits is also dwindling," notes Renew.

"In some cases parents might provide cash or share costs with grandparents," she says, but rarely do they enter official financial arrangements, she says.

She mentioned a 57-year-old grandmother from Sapphire, N.C., whom she worked with and who travels 44 miles five times a week to look after her daughter's three- and six-year-old children, as well as her son's 6-month-old son.

The woman quit her job as a nurse to provide child-care full-time to her grandchildren and relies on her husband's Social Security to get by. Yet she says the grandmother would rather pick up nursing shifts on the weekends than ask her kids for help, as she doesn't want to tap into their savings.

"She might ask her kids for financial support [if she has a health issue or an emergency] but that would be a last resort for her," says Renew.

Rebecca Parlakian, senior program officer at early-childhood-focused nonprofit Zero To Three, has similarly found that grandparents are reluctant to ask for payment.

Yet, because most first-time grandparents are in their 50s and still working, many reduce work hours or give up employment, she says.

When that is the case, she recommends being clear about hours of care they are able provide and where they can set boundaries in terms of costs and types of care.

"Talk through all the tricky questions," she says.

Check-ins every few months to see how the arrangement is going are also vital, she says.

"Grandparents may initially feel comfortable with one schedule but need to scale back," she says.

Seattle-based Maier agrees.

"Constant communication is one of the key elements that has made this arrangement successful," she says.

While initially she compensated her in-laws for their time and effort, they eventually asked to stop receiving payments. The grandparents continue to look after her kids, now aged six, four, and 15 months old.

"I feel very lucky to have family close by that we can rely on," she says, "My children have genuine and deep relationships with their grandparents due to their everyday presence in our lives," she says.

"I also think my in-laws have benefited both physically, mentally and emotionally," she adds.

data.title: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 Profit Rises 18% To Rs 757 Cr, AUM Grows 25%
data.description:
Housing finance company reports 18.3 per cent growth in total income to Rs 3,251 crore in Q2 FY27, while net interest income rises 10 per cent year-on-year

Bajaj Housing Finance reported an 18 per cent year-on-year increase in profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 757 crore for the second quarter of FY27, supported by growth in total income and assets under management (AUM).

The housing finance company had reported a profit after tax of Rs 643 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Total income increased 18.3 per cent to Rs 3,251 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 2,748 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.

Net interest income (NII), which represents the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 10 per cent to Rs 1,055 crore during the quarter, against Rs 956 crore in Q2 FY26.

Assets Under Management Rise 25 Per Cent

Bajaj Housing Finance's assets under management grew 25 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.58 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with Rs 1.27 lakh crore a year earlier.

The growth reflects an expansion in the company's lending portfolio during the quarter, with AUM crossing Rs 1.5 lakh crore.

Meanwhile, loan losses and provisions declined to Rs 35 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 43 crore in the corresponding period last year, indicating a reduction in the amount set aside against potential credit losses.

The September-quarter performance reflects continued growth in the company's earnings and managed assets, alongside lower loan-loss provisions.

data.title: Festive Housing Demand Turns Selective As Buyers Seek Value
data.description:
July-September sales point to resilient housing demand, but changing buyer preferences, premiumisation and affordability are reshaping festive-season purchases

India’s housing market is heading into the festive season with demand holding firm, but homebuyers are becoming more discerning about where and what they buy. Developer credibility, location, construction quality, connectivity and long-term value are increasingly shaping purchase decisions, signalling a shift from buying on festive sentiment alone to making more considered investments in residential property.

According to Anarock Research, housing sales across the top seven cities rose 3 per cent year-on-year to 1,00,220 units in July-September 2026, while sales value increased 2 per cent to Rs 1.55 lakh crore. Average residential prices climbed 7 per cent to Rs 9,714 per sq ft.

Are Buyers Returning With More Conviction?

The modest sales growth does not by itself capture the changing behaviour of buyers entering the festive market. Developers are seeing customers who are more willing to purchase, but are taking greater care over the developer, location and long-term usefulness of the property.

Ravi Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Lloyds Realty Developers Ltd., said the recent improvement should not be interpreted as a sharp festive surge. According to him, buyers who had postponed purchases are returning as confidence stabilises, particularly in established Mumbai neighbourhoods where they can upgrade without leaving familiar locations.

“It’s mostly underlying demand, with festive timing adding a lift. A 3 per cent rise is too modest to call a festive surge,” Agarwal said. He added that the quarter after Diwali would provide a clearer indication of whether the recovery is structural, with redevelopment benefiting from demand for better homes in established localities.

Pradeep Aggarwal, Founder and Chairman, Signature Global (India) Ltd., sees stronger end-user fundamentals behind the current market. He said improved income visibility and a growing preference for home ownership among young professionals are supporting purchase decisions, particularly among buyers looking for credible developers.

“The foundation is also end-user driven, supported by improved income visibility and a growing preference for home ownership among young professionals,” Aggarwal said. He added that buyers in the NCR are increasingly choosing developers with strong delivery records, while micro-markets such as Southern Peripheral Road, Dwarka Expressway, Sohna and Gurugram West are attracting demand.

What Are Buyers Actually Paying For?

The changing buyer is perhaps most visible in the premium segment, where purchasing decisions are increasingly moving beyond headline price and apartment size. Buyers are assessing the experience a property offers and whether its design, location and execution justify the overall cost.

Sidharth Chowdhry, Managing Director, Dalcore, said luxury buyers are becoming more informed and are placing greater emphasis on the character and quality of a residence. Architecture, privacy, functionality and craftsmanship are emerging as differentiators as buyers look beyond conventional amenity packages.

“Today’s luxury homebuyer is increasingly informed and selective, placing greater emphasis on the quality and character of a residence rather than price or size alone,” Chowdhry said. He added that developers need to respond with homes reflecting architectural intent, thoughtful use of space and craftsmanship rather than relying on standardised luxury features.

Himanshu Luthra, Managing Director, Divine Vision Infra, said the same scrutiny is extending beyond the luxury segment. Buyers are increasingly assessing whether a property makes practical and financial sense over the long term, with location and connectivity becoming important alongside documentation and construction quality.

“Buyers want a good location, good connectivity, clear legal papers and long-term worth before they buy,” Luthra said. He added that festive sentiment may accelerate decisions, but sustained demand will depend on genuine end-user interest and confidence in the project and its developer.

Is Premiumisation Changing The Shape Of Demand?

The shift towards higher-value homes is visible in the market data, but it also raises questions about who is being left behind. Knight Frank’s January-September 2026 data shows homes priced above Rs 1 crore accounted for 55 per cent of sales, up from 50 per cent a year earlier.

Shekhar Patel, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Ganesh Housing Ltd. and National President of CREDAI, said premiumisation should not automatically be read as a wholesale shift towards luxury housing. Rising land and construction costs are pushing reasonably sized homes beyond the existing affordable-housing threshold.

“Premiumization is partly a classification problem,” Patel said, pointing to the Rs 45 lakh affordable housing cap, which has remained unchanged since 2017. He added that demand for 60–90 sq m homes remains resilient, particularly in Ahmedabad, suggesting that affordability constraints are partly being created by the way housing categories are defined.

Ankita Luharuka, CEO, Alliance City Developers, said premiumisation is also forcing developers to rethink how products are planned for different buyer groups. The objective, she said, should be to provide the right combination of configuration, space, amenities and connectivity without pushing the overall purchase cost beyond the target customer’s reach.

“Developers need to adopt a more differentiated approach to product planning,” Luharuka said. She added that pricing should reflect local market conditions and project value, while milestone-linked payment plans and structured buying options can help customers manage cash flows without relying on large discounts.

The festive season is therefore revealing a housing market where demand is not simply returning in greater volume, but becoming more considered in quality. Buyers are weighing credibility, location, design, affordability and long-term value more closely, forcing developers to compete on relevance rather than festive incentives alone.

data.title: IIFCL, Two Coal India Units Eye FY27 Listings, DIPAM Chief Says
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields has filed its draft IPO prospectus, while the government is preparing India Infrastructure Finance Company and South Eastern Coalfields for listing in the current financial year

The Centre is targeting stock market listings for India Infrastructure Finance Company (IIFCL) and two Coal India subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL) and South Eastern Coalfields (SECL), in FY27, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla said, according to media reports.

The planned listings follow the stock market debuts of Coal India subsidiaries BCCL in January 2026 and CMPDI in March 2026.

IPO Preparations Under Way

The government has begun preparations for IIFCL’s initial public offering, inviting bids to appoint a registrar and share transfer agent, as well as an advertising agency for the proposed issue. Eligible bidders can submit applications online until November 3, according to the report. MCL has already filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), while SECL is also slated for listing during the financial year.

The three offerings will have different implications for government receipts. Proceeds from IIFCL’s IPO will accrue directly to the Centre, its sole shareholder. Proceeds from stake sales in MCL and SECL will go to Coal India, their parent company, with the government potentially benefiting indirectly through dividends in FY28.

IIFCL’s Financial Performance

Wholly owned by the Centre, IIFCL was established in 2006 to provide long-term financial assistance to viable infrastructure projects. It registered with the Reserve Bank of India as an infrastructure finance non-banking financial company in 2013. The company had a net worth of Rs 17,898 crore at the end of FY26. Its net profit fell 36 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,379 crore in FY26, weighed down by mark-to-market losses on offshore borrowings amid foreign exchange fluctuations.

Coal India Units’ Production And Profits

MCL was Coal India’s largest-producing subsidiary in FY26, with output of 218.31 million tonnes and net profit of Rs 10,698 crore. SECL produced 176.29 million tonnes during the year and reported net profit of Rs 4,755 crore. Coal India’s total production declined to 768.19 million tonnes in FY26 from 781.06 million tonnes a year earlier. Its consolidated profit after tax fell to Rs 31,071 crore from Rs 35,450 crore, while revenue from operations was broadly stable at Rs 1,68,400 crore, compared with Rs 1,69,177 crore in FY25.

Government Disinvestment Target

The proposed listings form part of the Centre’s broader disinvestment and asset monetisation programme. The government has raised Rs 62,124 crore in FY27 so far and has effectively met its Rs 80,000 crore target for miscellaneous capital receipts after including around Rs 26,500 crore expected from the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank, which is nearing completion. The planned offerings would mark a resumption of government IPOs after more than two years. The last such offering was the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) IPO in FY24, when the government sold a 10 per cent stake.

data.title: Reliance Says Jio Satellite Services Also Await India Clearances
data.description:
Reliance Industries responds to Elon Musk’s criticism of Starlink’s delayed India entry, saying Jio’s satellite services are also awaiting government approvals and all applicants must follow the same rules

Reliance Industries on Friday, 16 October, said its Jio satellite services were still awaiting government clearances, responding to Elon Musk’s allegations that powerful business interests were impeding Starlink’s entry into India. The company said domestic and foreign applicants must follow the same regulatory process.

The exchange brings the regulatory hurdles facing satellite broadband operators into focus as Elon Musk’s Starlink seeks to enter India’s internet market, where Reliance Jio is an established telecom player. Reliance said it welcomed competition, including from Starlink, and cited Jio’s growth since its commercial entry into India’s telecom market in 2016.

Reliance Says All Applicants Must Follow The Same Rules

In a statement posted on X, Reliance said India welcomed investment and innovation from domestic and international companies, provided they operated within the law. It said the government had stated that the same process applied to every applicant, irrespective of whether the company was Indian or foreign. “Jio’s own satellite services await clearances,” Reliance said, adding that it had never feared competition and viewed it as a test of which company served customers better. The statement did not identify each pending approval or specify a launch date for Jio’s satellite services.

Musk Accuses Powerful Business Interests Of Blocking Starlink

The response followed a series of social media posts by Musk, the chief executive of SpaceX, which operates Starlink. Musk alleged that powerful business interests were blocking the satellite internet service’s entry into India to protect existing market positions. He also addressed Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani sarcastically as “Prime Minister Ambani” in a post seeking access to the Indian market.

Starlink’s proposed entry has drawn attention because satellite broadband could expand internet access in areas where conventional connectivity is limited. Musk has argued that the service could help connect underserved communities, while the Indian government has maintained that operators must satisfy the applicable regulatory and security requirements before beginning commercial operations.

Jio Cites 530 Million Customers Since 2016 Entry

Reliance also pointed to Jio’s record in the telecom market as evidence of its approach to competition. The company said Jio entered India’s crowded telecom sector in 2016 with no customers and had built a base of more than 530 million customers over the following decade. The statement did not provide a specific timeline for the launch of Jio’s satellite internet services. Its response focused on equal treatment of applicants, compliance with Indian laws, and the company’s stated willingness to compete with international operators.

data.title: Diesel Sales Jump 25% As Festive Demand Lifts Fuel Use
data.description:
State-run fuel retailers sold 3.65 million tonnes in the first half of October as festival-linked transport demand, agricultural use and lower pump prices boosted diesel purchases

Diesel sales surged 25.4 per cent year-on-year in the first half of October, as festive-season transport activity and agricultural demand lifted fuel consumption, preliminary industry data showed on Friday. State-run oil marketing companies sold 3.65 million tonnes of diesel during 1 to 15 October, with purchases also supported by lower retail prices than those offered by private fuel retailers.

The increase comes as global diesel prices climb amid supply disruptions linked to the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. While state-run retailers have kept pump prices unchanged since May, private operators have raised prices and redirected fuel towards export markets, creating a price gap that is drawing customers towards public-sector outlets.

Festive Transport And Agricultural Demand Support Sales

Diesel demand has benefited from increased trucking during the festival season, as wholesalers build inventories ahead of Diwali in November. SP Singh, a senior fellow at the Indian Foundation of Transport Research and Training, attributed the rise to stronger agricultural demand and higher transportation activity. Farmers also use diesel-powered generator sets for irrigation, adding to consumption.

Truck sales provide another indicator of stronger transport activity. Sales rose to 44,323 units in September, an increase of 33.57 per cent from August, according to Singh. Wholesalers' inventory-building ahead of the festival period has contributed to higher trucking activity, he said.

State-Run Retailers Gain From Price Gap

Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation have kept retail fuel prices unchanged since May, despite higher global fuel prices. The three state-run companies are absorbing losses of around Rs 20 per litre on diesel sales, according to Prashant Vasisht, senior vice-president at rating agency ICRA.

Private retailers Nayara Energy and Reliance Industries have raised fuel prices and are exporting products to benefit from stronger international margins. Diesel at private fuel stations is around Rs 5 per litre costlier than at state-run outlets, while petrol is Rs 3 per litre more expensive, according to the report. The price differential has encouraged some customers to switch to public-sector retailers.

Gasoline Sales Also Edge Higher

State-run retailers' gasoline sales rose to 1.55 million tonnes during 1 to 15 October, up 0.9 per cent from the same period in September. The increase was considerably smaller than the growth recorded in diesel sales over the same period.

Diesel is also being used to generate electricity amid rising power demand, Vasisht said. The latest sales figures reflect the combined impact of seasonal consumption, agricultural requirements and the shift towards state-run outlets offering lower retail prices.

data.title: Motorola’s Signature 27 Is An All-out Flagship Bet In A Shrinking Market, Says Shivam Ranjan
data.description:
Motorola’s APAC Marketing Head sheds light on memory-led price inflation, Lenovo’s supply-chain advantage and why seven years of updates is now hygiene for flagship buyers

India’s smartphone market is going through one of its toughest stretches in years. Shipments fell 10 per cent year-on-year in the April to June quarter of 2026, the steepest June-quarter decline in six years, with soaring memory costs pushing up prices across nearly every segment and leading many buyers to delay upgrades. The entry-level segment took the biggest hit, while vivo held the top spot with an 18 per cent share.

The slide began earlier. In Q1, shipments fell 3 per cent, the weakest quarter in six years, and more than 80 models saw average price hikes of 15 per cent. Counterpoint now expects the market to shrink by 13 per cent over the full year, with manufacturers leaning on premium devices, financing offers and portfolio changes until component costs ease.

Premium is the one pocket holding up. That makes this a telling moment for flagship silicon. At Snapdragon Summit 2026, Qualcomm unveiled the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and a higher-end Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, both built on a 2nm process. Both chips reach clock speeds of up to 5GHz, and the Extreme variant gets the bigger AI leap, with a 35 per cent gain over the Gen 5 against 14 per cent for the standard chip. Xiaomi and Motorola were the first to show phones powered by the new chips at the event.

Motorola’s entry is the Signature 27, built around the Extreme chip and pitched as the company’s most ambitious phone yet. On the sidelines of India Mobile Congress 2026, where the Signature 27 was shown to India, we spoke to Shivam Ranjan, APAC Marketing Head, Motorola Mobility. We covered what makes the phone stand out, how Motorola is handling the memory crunch, who the buyer is, and why software support has become table stakes.

Here are the edited excerpts:

Tell us about the new phone. What makes the Signature 27 stand out?

While we have not formally announced the phone globally yet, that will happen soon, within 2026, for both India and the world. We are here to support our partner Qualcomm, which is announcing its latest chipsets, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the 8 Elite. This will be one of the first phones globally to come with the Extreme Gen 6, so we are here to share a few glimpses.

The first reason it stands out is that we have been making mobile phones since 1973, and we can comfortably say this is the best phone we have ever made. That is not just about performance. It cuts across the device, including imaging. We redefined imaging when we introduced the Signature last year, and this year we are taking it a notch higher with the latest camera technology and Qualcomm’s chipset.

On agentic capabilities, taking consumer intent to action, this device will bring use cases that today are truly imaginary. You will see incredible performance, gaming and connectivity. With six antennas, you get breakthrough connectivity, and download speeds go up by more than 25 per cent, which also helps cloud AI models and your overall agentic AI experience.

On software, there is a promise of seven years of OS upgrades and security patches. All of this comes with a redesigned language: an aluminium silhouette with curved contours, with ceramic and brushed aluminium, and a completely differentiated camera module. This is the best of what you can do with a smartphone.

Memory-led inflation has pushed up smartphone prices globally, and TSMC is raising chip manufacturing prices too. How does the market evolve, and how does India adapt?

This is a category-wide issue, not limited to any geography. It comes from the AI boom, with demand outstripping the supply of memory, and other components are seeing an impact too. Everyone in the industry feels it.

But Motorola is far better equipped than some other OEMs to manage this, because of the might of the Lenovo ecosystem. Lenovo is the number one PC manufacturer, so our supply chain and procurement are in a far better position to secure what is needed for each market, including India.

The markets will keep evolving. We are seeing an impact, and volumes are shrinking. But the adaptation we are seeing is a premium movement. Consumers are moving up the price ladder because they pay for products where they see value, not necessarily to hit a particular price point.

When you say you are well equipped, do you mean you accept that prices will stay high, or that you will wait it out until they come down?

There is no question of waiting it out. What I mean is that our parent company is the largest PC manufacturer in the world, so we are well equipped to secure supplies for our products, including Motorola. There is no concern that we will not have enough supply in the market. We are well positioned to handle the situation.

It is also not something any single OEM can change. We are here to stay and to participate in the market, and there is no question of pausing. You can see that with the Signature 27 and the other products you will see soon. What we can assure consumers is that we will stay competitive and give them more value where it is required. That is how we differentiate.

Who is the buyer for this phone? The first Signature was one of the best phones of the year and came in under Rs 60,000. Rumours put this one at around Rs 90,000.

I won’t comment on pricing. But last year’s Signature was our first attempt at a candy bar flagship, and we deliberately kept it at entry-flagship price points because we first needed to gain acceptance in that segment.

With the Signature 27, we have gone for an all-out flagship. It is the Ultra when it comes to everything. It has things you do not see with other brands, such as Bang & Olufsen audio, exclusive to us on this device. The design language is innovative, and the chipset, camera, and agentic experiences are the latest and the greatest. We kept what people liked about the first Signature. When we introduced it, one of the questions you had was why we did not go for the Elite chipset. We have addressed that with this one, for people who wanted the best of the best.

The buyer is someone who wants to challenge the status quo and ask why they should keep buying the same brands. That is a tech-first buyer, an early adopter and an innovation enthusiast, someone who is design-first too, but truly a flagship buyer.

Is it safe to say you are done with the affordable flagship segment?

I wouldn’t say that. We are not giving up any segment. Our attempt is to offer consumers a viable option at every price point, and last year’s Signature played the affordable flagship role for us.

As we move along, that role may be filled by a product from another franchise, or by a product within the Signature franchise. Last year’s Signature also has time to go. We do not plan to end it soon, and as you said yourself, you still love the product. It is extremely competitive, and there is a segment of buyers looking for an affordable or entry-level flagship. We let that product play that game.

You are offering seven years of OS updates. Is that a primary concern for Indian buyers?

With flagship devices, consumers now take this as hygiene. They want a worry-free, peace-of-mind experience for as long as they plan to keep the phone. It will not necessarily get you higher sales, but if you do not offer it, you create question marks.

It is a need-to-have to cut ice with this cohort. If you do not have it, you do not even cross the threshold. If you do have it, you do not get an additional premium for it. So we are making sure we give what a flagship consumer asks for and deserves.
